It works for a lot less money than the true tool. - You MUST have some type of spanner tool like this. No normal wrench is going to work. You can get the proper tool for ~$50, or get this which is a bit big for the WH2X1193 Hub Nut. It worked though, and even though it's larger than the nut it didn't damage the nut. We took turns beating it to death for probably a half hour with a heavy hammer and several applications of penetrating oil (small mallet sledge would have been better). Not much room to swing but eventually it starts turning more and more. Kept one hand on the tool to keep it in place. Because it's two pieces which just seemed like more problems I glued mine together with Goop glue (stays flexible, so it survived the hammering).

Ended up replacing the nut because the threads were corroded. The gasket seal was completely corroded. There is metal inside it which was rusted through. The split washer was ok (scraped off mineral deposits). The chromed flat washer seemed ok (slight loss of the plating with some corrosion).

Some huge issues. But good ice - The ice is great but there are several issues that make this a terrible device. First, it's Bluetooth. Not wifi. Don't know why but it's like that on every device.
You can set a schedule which is good for about 3 days. However if you touch the device at all. Push the button for more ice, or absolutely anything. It kills your schedule. Meaning to go to grab ice the next day you have none.
Sometimes you set the schedule back and it starts up hours before or after because it has no internal clock. And you can't manually set the clock.
Now if you start it manually, for whatever reason, or stop it. And you want to turn the schedule back on.. You can't because it will stop it/start it again! To have to wait an hour or two until your Ice is made or the schedule is off.
So the basics are the the ice is great. Absolutely everything else about this is like it was designed by someone who did absolutely zero testing.
I really can't give something so poorly designed a good review.

Exactly what I was looking for! - I bought this to replace an old yellowed vent cover on an existing vent fan in our newly painted bathroom. I struggled for a long time to decide on which replacement vent cover to buy - I didn't know the make/model of the existing fan, and none of the replacement covers at the "big box" stores were big enough. My opening was approximately 9x9 inches, so I figured that I needed a 10x10 vent cover to cover the drywall gaps on either side. I also needed a cover that had the V-type spring clips (my clip slots were about 7.5 inches apart). After staring at that stupid ugly uncovered vent fan for months, I decided that this replacement cover seemed like the best option, and took the plunge, half expecting it not to work. I am pleased to say that it was exactly what I needed! Installation was super easy - just insert one prong of the V-clip into the hole first, then squeeze and insert the other. Took more time to get out the ladder than to install the cover. The cover is white, not off-white, and looks great against the white ceiling. Interestingly, the small embossed rectangle in the lower corner that looks like it should contain a brand name is blank. Overall, I am very pleased with this purchase, and only wish I would have done it months ago!

A fraction of the repair cost compared to calling an appliance guy! - We have an old Caloric brand wall oven that came with the house. I have no idea how old it is, but within a year or two of living here, the oven stopped working. It would glow, but no gas would come out and it would never start. I called an appliance repair man who determined it was a bad ignitor. He explained to me that the gas won't turn on until the ignitor reaches a certain temp, so either the ignitor wasn't getting hot enough, or it wasn't sending the signal to turn on the gas when it did. Either way, the problem was entirely with the ignitor. He replaced it, and something like $200 later, the oven was back to working. Until it stopped working again about a year after that. This time it didn't even glow, the oven would just do nothing.

Instead of another expensive repair, I decided on a hunch to assume the part the repair man brought was lower quality than the original. I looked it up online and found a match here on Amazon. I felt confident that I could swap it myself now that I saw the repair guy do it, and sure enough this did the trick for a fraction of what I would pay him to come back! Its been a little over a month since putting it in, and so far so good. I'm hoping this will last longer than the last one, but even if it doesn't, worst case scenario is that I'll spend $20-30 on an annual repair until we can afford to replace the whole oven! I can deal with that.

I’ve been making cold brew in a French press until now, and I have been pleased with the results, but since it requires hands on filtering, I thought this OXO system would simplify the filtering and allow the machine to do most of the work. Wrong.
With a French Press, once the coffee has brewed, I can press the coffee and separate most of the grounds from the cold brew. Then I slowly pour it out into a mesh filter lined with a paper filter and wait for it to slowly seep through. I have to change the paper filter half way through before pouring the second half.
With this OXO system, you are supposed to be able to flip the switch and the cold brew will drip down in to the glass carafe below. But the grounds kept clogging the filter and then absolutely no liquid could get through. (I will also note that I have a quality conical burr grinder, so the grind should not be an issue.) I had to stand over it for about 15 min scraping the grounds to the side or scooping spoonfuls of grounds out of the brewing container. After 15 minutes of this, we were left with roughly 2/3 of the volume of cold brew we would have gotten from the same recipe in a French press. The reduced volume was partially due to me scooping grounds out of the way and throwing them in the sink, and partially because there was no way to effectively press the liquid out of the grounds. Also the taste was inferior. Again probably because the most concentrated cold brew couldn’t be pressed out of the grounds.
Overall the taste was nowhere as good and the process was more cumbersome than a French press. I wish I loved this machine, but on the plus side, it’s one less thing to sit on my counter and take up more space in the fridge.
